identity: Highcourt is safe inside its walls; outside them, private collectors dress their charges as royal tolls.

quests.title: A Hearing for the Absent
quests.text: [PH] Chapter 1 (The Accord): the capital's envoy has a reported case of people and loads entered in the wrong ledger and sends the player to The Charter of Stone's leader at the Miner's Guild house of this capital. Real text to follow.
quests.completion: [PH] Alis Cartwright: she asks who really needs a load and who drives it, and takes up the case. Real text to follow.

variants.text: [PH] Mariel Waybook: word from Goldmead says people and supplies are being claimed under a capital toll mark; Alis Cartwright at the Miner's Guild house can check the transport pledges. A reported case: Mariel does not claim the player helped Pella. Real text to follow.
variants.completion: [PH] Alis Cartwright: she asks who really needs a load and who drives it, and takes up the case. Real text to follow.

variants.text: [PH] Dorrin Gateledger: a Counting House stamp turns up on stolen ore bags; Hadrin Beamset at the Miner's Guild house checks how it ties to the workings and the supply. A reported case: Dorrin does not claim the player helped Tovin. Real text to follow.
variants.completion: [PH] Hadrin Beamset: he asks which work stands still without the material and whether everybody came back, and takes up the case. Real text to follow.

variants.text: [PH] Eriath Boughwarden: the Bough Seal is passed off as leave to take; Caelir Veinward at the Miner's Guild house knows the limits of the releases it covers. A reported case: Eriath does not claim the player helped Nima. Real text to follow.
variants.completion: [PH] Caelir Veinward: she asks exactly what a release allows, and takes up the case. Real text to follow.

quests.lesson: Chapter 1 opens at the envoy at 19 with no prerequisite; a walk to the capital's Miner's Guild house.

quests.title: What a Seal Allows
quests.text: [PH] Chapter 1 (The Accord): the guild has halted a suspect delivery in the capital; the player secures its record at the spot and brings it back, and the leader decides the case. Real text to follow.
quests.completion: [PH] Alis Cartwright: she compares the record with the agreed delivery, rejects the extension and releases the load to its right recipient. A confirmed load gives nobody a say over the people beside it. Where the papers came from stays open; a like case waits at Frostbarrow Shelf. Real text to follow.

variants.text: [PH] Alis Cartwright: a delivery for the joint supply waits in the yard beside the butcher's shop. Its covering record stretches the drivers' duty as if the workers could be put under another order along with the load. Alis has halted it; secure the record there and bring it back. Real text to follow.
variants.completion: [PH] Alis Cartwright: she compares the record with the agreed delivery, rejects the extension and releases the load to its right recipient. A confirmed load gives nobody a say over the people beside it. Where the papers came from stays open; a like case waits at Frostbarrow Shelf. Real text to follow.

variants.text: [PH] Hadrin Beamset: tool material stands on the loading apron of the ore yard. Its acceptance was tied to a claimed transfer of the crew it was meant for, so their own supply would count as delivered. Hadrin never approved it; secure the load record there and bring it back. Real text to follow.
variants.completion: [PH] Hadrin Beamset: with the supply he sets out which crew the material was meant for and has it issued to them. A clean stamp replaces neither a sound order nor safe working. Where the papers came from stays open; a like case waits at Frostbarrow Shelf. Real text to follow.

variants.text: [PH] Caelir Veinward: material for a limited tending and repair job waits at the timber check beside the bowyer's workshop. A covering sheet turns the release into a wider claim on timber and on the tenders' labour. Secure the sheet there and bring it back. Real text to follow.
variants.completion: [PH] Caelir Veinward: she confirms the true purpose and strikes the extension. Leave to tend is no leave to clear-cut, nor a say over the tenders. Where the papers came from stays open; a like case waits at Frostbarrow Shelf. Real text to follow.

quests.lesson: A spot in the capital town (a town place) and back; the leader decides the capital's case, the papers' source stays open.

quests.title: The Dead Cannot Owe Toll
quests.text: Debtbound Zombies wander the {name:commons}, which lies {zone_area:commons}, still burdened with somebody's unpaid tolls. Put five to rest after dark. Penn's name keeps appearing in the complaints, and I intend to learn why; in the meantime, the dead have paid quite enough.
quests.lesson: Night work near the capital; zombies burn at dawn.

quests.title: An Arrow Is Not a Receipt
quests.text: The complaints lead to Toll Archers in the {name:deer_park} {dir_of:highcourt:deer_park}, collecting after dark from anyone unfortunate enough to pass. Defeat five there at night. Their badges claim royal authority; the crown's instructions do not include shooting customers.
quests.lesson: Ranged night roster in a forest; daytime there is quiet.

quests.title: Optional: Tithes After Dark
quests.text: The petitions now include Tithe Revenants in the {name:orchards}, which lie {zone_area:orchards}. They rise at night to demand payments nobody remembers owing. Lay five of them to rest after dark. I would prefer the dead stop collecting before the living start believing them.
quests.lesson: Optional: a night hunt beside the day orchard work.

quests.title: The Last Unauthorised Stamp
quests.text: {name:tollmaster_penn} conducts his business at the {name:toll_camp} {dir_from_giver:toll_camp}, with enough borrowed ceremony to embarrass a coronation. Defeat five Toll Archers there and then Penn himself; his camp operates day and night. Keep clear of the other archers while you close on each one. I want him to discover that stamping a demand does not make it lawful.
quests.lesson: Archer camp plus its named normal leader.

quests.title: A Peg for the Bread Board
quests.text: My bread board rocks, and the royal kitchen has offered to lend me a peg with more conditions than a peace treaty. Bring me one Gnarled Boar Tusk from a Furrow Boar by day on the {name:commons}, which lies {zone_area:commons}. Their yellow names mean they only fight back when struck. I would rather settle the matter with the boar.
quests.lesson: A daytime errand that leaves your enchant stock alone.

quests.title: Optional: The Long Table
quests.text: The palace has ordered venison for a banquet and left the hunting to whoever happens to be standing near my oven. Bring down six Fallow Bucks by day on the {name:commons}. Their yellow names mean they only fight back when struck, which is more patience than the banquet guests will show.
quests.lesson: Optional: neutral daytime game, the minor role on the capital commons.

quests.title: Pies Have Consequences
quests.text: The palace expects fruit pies, while the pickers expect to keep their fingers; I find the second request entirely reasonable. Hunt five Dog-Foxes by day in the {name:orchards}, which lie {zone_area:orchards}. Mind their red names: they start fights, unlike the Orchard Foxes sharing that ground.
quests.lesson: Aggressive and neutral foxes share one orchard.

quests.title: The Empty River Baskets
quests.text: I paid for river baskets and received a very confident promise, which has proved difficult to put bread in. Find Merren Oakstamp at Whitebridge Market Close in Whitebridge Shire and ask what became of my order. Follow the road, or visit the stables about a mount if your feet have already lodged a complaint.

quests.title: Bread for the March
quests.text: The watch at Cinderline eats my bread and stands between the Accord's homes and the fighting. Go to Cinderline Watch in Ashenward March and speak with Toren Waterbarrel; tell him the person who dealt with Penn is ready to help. Get yourself to level 30 before making the journey into contested country. Eat before you leave, too; courage is no breakfast.
